operators.name: Banglalink
operators.note: MSISDNs are addressed as tel:880XXXXXXXXXX. The platform's published samples use 88019… and 88014… numbers. Confirm in the portal which operators your application is provisioned for before assuming reach.

baseUrls.configuration: Configure one URL per provisioned service (APPLINK_SMS_SEND_URL, APPLINK_USSD_SEND_URL, …). An unset endpoint means that API is not enabled on the application, and the client should refuse to call it rather than fail with E1309 at the platform. See templates/.env.example.
baseUrls.egressIpNote: Applink publishes no IP-echo endpoint of its own. Any public echo service works — run it on the server that will make the calls, not on a laptop.

auth.note: Every outbound request carries applicationId and password in the JSON body. There are no headers, tokens or signatures. The password is the API key emailed to the registered address when the application is approved.

rules: Always tel:-prefixed. Send tel:8801959979376 — the form used by the subscription, OTP and CaaS samples.

The published SMS samples write the same address as tel:+8801959979376. Both forms appear in the platform's own documentation; normalise to one in a single helper and, if an SMS send returns E1325, try the other form and report it to support.
May be a masked value when number masking is provisioned. Treat it as opaque — do not parse it, strip it, or assume a length.
tel:all broadcasts to the entire subscribed base (SMS send only).

wireTypes.rule: Every request value is a JSON string — amount, action, version, encoding, deliveryStatusRequest, otp, sessionId and every identifier included. destinationAddresses and subscriberIds are arrays of strings; applicationMetaData is an object of strings. Never send a number, a boolean or null, and omit an optional field rather than sending it empty.
wireTypes.version: version is a parameter of SMS Send and USSD Send only. The subscription, OTP and CaaS requests do not carry it — follow each endpoint's parameter list, not a shared template.
wireTypes.names: Field names are case-sensitive and differ between endpoints on purpose: Currency (CaaS OTP Generation) vs currency (Query Balance), destinationAddresses (SMS, array) vs destinationAddress (USSD, string), subscriberIds (charging info, array) vs subscriberId (everything else), and sourceAddress for the subscriber on CaaS OTP Verification.

responseEnvelope.criticalNote: Applink returns HTTP 200 for application-level failures. Branch on statusCode, never on the HTTP status alone. S1000 is success; P1003 on CaaS OTP generation means the OTP was dispatched and the charge is not complete yet.
reading: Decide the outcome from statusCode alone, against the outcome that endpoint is expected to return — S1000 for most, P1003 for CaaS OTP Generation.

When statusCode is anything else, rely on statusCode and statusDetail only. The endpoint's own fields (requestCorrelator, referenceNo, baseSize, destinationResponses, subscriptionStatus …) may be absent from a failure.

Every response value is a string, numbers included (baseSize, chargeableBalance, amounts). Parse at the boundary — an integer for baseSize, a decimal type for money — and accept a bare number too, so a platform-side change cannot break the parser.
Read every field other than statusCode with a default, and ignore fields you do not recognise rather than failing on them.

conventions.platformNameNote: requestId and sessionId are described in the documentation as unique 'within TAP' — the telco application platform that Applink runs on. It is the same system; quote those identifiers to support.

services.name: SMS Send
services.summary: Send an MT (Mobile Terminated) SMS to one or more subscribers.

parameters.name: version
parameters.description: API version, numbered 1.0, 2.0 and so on. If specified in the request the same version is returned in the response; if omitted the latest version is used.

parameters.name: applicationId
parameters.description: Identifies the application. Unique identifier generated when the application is provisioned. Only a single value per request.

parameters.name: password
parameters.description: The API key sent to your registered email address when the application was approved.

parameters.name: message
parameters.description: Content of the message to send. Messages over the limit are broken up by the platform before sending.

parameters.name: destinationAddresses
parameters.description: Array of tel:-prefixed destination addresses. Always an array, even for one recipient. tel:all sends to the subscribed base of the application. May be a masked value depending on the application type.

parameters.name: sourceAddress
parameters.exampleNote: must be an alias provisioned on your application — any other value is E1331
parameters.description: Address the message appears to come from — a provisioned alias such as a shortcode, or a tel:-prefixed address.

parameters.name: deliveryStatusRequest
parameters.exampleNote: set "1" only once your SMS delivery-report callback URL is configured
parameters.description: 0 = delivery report not required, 1 = delivery report required. A delivery report arrives at your SMS report callback URL.

parameters.name: encoding
parameters.description: Encoding scheme used in the message. 0 = Text, 240 = Flash SMS, 245 = Binary. Defaults to Text. With Binary the message content must be hex encoded.

parameters.name: binaryHeader
parameters.description: Hex-encoded binary header, for advanced message types where the header is supplied by the application. Only meaningful with encoding 245.

responseFields.name: version
responseFields.description: API version echoed from the request.

responseFields.name: requestId
responseFields.description: Uniquely identifies this request within the platform. Persist it — support traces on it, and delivery reports carry it.

responseFields.name: destinationResponses
responseFields.description: One entry per address in the request. A multi-recipient send can partially succeed, so branch on each entry's statusCode, not only the top-level one.

fields.name: timeStamp
fields.description: When the platform processed this recipient.

fields.name: address
fields.description: The tel:-prefixed recipient this entry reports on.

fields.name: messageId
fields.description: Per-recipient message identifier.

fields.name: statusCode
fields.description: Outcome for this recipient alone.

fields.name: statusDetail
fields.description: Human-readable outcome for this recipient.

responseFields.name: statusCode
responseFields.description: The status code for the entire request. S1000 on success.

responseFields.name: statusDetail
responseFields.description: Description of the status for the entire request.

responseHandling.outcome: The platform accepted the send. Delivery is a separate event, reported on the delivery-status callback if you asked for one.
persist: requestId — delivery reports and support trace on it
responseHandling.next: Branch on every destinationResponses entry's statusCode as well: a top-level S1000 with a failed entry is a partial send, and only that recipient should be retried or dropped.

wrongFields.destinationAddress: SMS Send takes destinationAddresses — plural, and always an array. The singular string form belongs to USSD Send.
wrongFields.to: The recipients go in destinationAddresses, an array of tel: addresses.
wrongFields.text: The message body goes in message.

rules: destinationAddresses is always an array, even for a single recipient.
Guard tel:all behind a deliberate, separately-authorised code path, and check the base size first.
sourceAddress must be a provisioned alias — an arbitrary value fails with E1331.
Only set deliveryStatusRequest to 1 if you consume the SMS report callback.
Keep under 160 GSM-7 characters for a single part. Bangla text is UCS-2, so budget 70 characters per part; the platform splits longer messages and each part is charged.
The published sample writes the destination as tel:+8801959979376. Send tel:8801959979376 for consistency with every other Applink API, and normalise in one helper.

services.name: USSD Send
services.summary: Send a USSD screen to a handset inside an open session.

parameters.name: version
parameters.description: API version, numbered 1.0, 2.0 and so on. If specified in the request the same version is returned in the response.

parameters.name: applicationId
parameters.description: Identifies the application. Unique identifier generated when the application is provisioned. Only a single value per request.

parameters.name: password
parameters.description: The API key sent to your registered email address when the application was approved.

parameters.name: message
parameters.description: Content of the message sent by the application — the screen text the subscriber sees.

parameters.name: sessionId
parameters.description: Unique number the USSD gateway assigns to the application for the duration of the session. It is maintained across every message in a single session — echo the one you were given, never generate your own.

parameters.name: ussdOperation
parameters.description: USSD operation. The application assigns mt-init when it initiates a session, mt-cont for any message that follows an init, and mt-fin when the session ends on a final message. mo-init and mo-cont are assigned by the platform on inbound messages.

parameters.name: destinationAddress
parameters.description: Destination address — a tel:-prefixed telephone number, which may be a masked value depending on the application type.

parameters.name: encoding
parameters.description: Encoding scheme used in the message. 440 = plain ASCII characters.

responseFields.name: version
responseFields.description: API version echoed from the request.

responseFields.name: requestId
responseFields.description: Uniquely identifies this request within the platform.

responseFields.name: timeStamp
responseFields.description: Processed timestamp.

responseFields.name: statusCode
responseFields.description: The status code for the entire request. S1000 on success.

responseFields.name: statusDetail
responseFields.description: Description of the status for the entire request.

sampleRequest.message:
1. Press One
2. Press two
3. Press three
4. Exit

responseHandling.outcome: The screen was handed to the USSD gateway for this session.
persist: requestId — for the log line, alongside sessionId
responseHandling.next: After mt-cont, the subscriber's reply arrives on the USSD receive callback as mo-cont. After mt-fin the session is over and nothing more arrives.

wrongFields.destinationAddresses: USSD Send takes destinationAddress — one tel: address as a string. The plural array form belongs to SMS Send.
wrongFields.sourceAddress: Address the screen to the subscriber with destinationAddress — the sourceAddress you received on the USSD receive callback, sent back unchanged.

rules: Echo the sessionId the platform sent you. A sessionId you invented orphans the session and the subscriber sees nothing.
End terminal screens with mt-fin. Continuing to send mt-cont leaves the session hanging until the network times it out.
Screens are plain ASCII (encoding 440) — no emoji, no Bangla script, no smart quotes. Sanitise generated text before sending.
Keep each screen under about 160 characters and the tree two or three levels deep. Sessions time out in seconds.
Never charge inline inside a USSD session. Acknowledge with mt-fin, charge asynchronously, and SMS the result.

services.name: Subscription Register
services.summary: Opt a subscriber in to the application. Same endpoint as unregister, with action "1".

parameters.name: applicationId
parameters.description: Identifies the application. Unique identifier generated when the application is provisioned. Only a single value per request.

parameters.name: password
parameters.description: The API key sent to your registered email address when the application was approved.

parameters.name: subscriberId
parameters.description: The subscriber's tel:-prefixed MSISDN, a unique identifier. May be a masked value depending on the application type. Only a single value per request.

parameters.name: action
parameters.description: 0 = user unsubscription, 1 = user subscription. Sent as a string.

responseFields.name: version
responseFields.description: API version.

responseFields.name: statusCode
responseFields.description: The status code for the entire request.

responseFields.name: statusDetail
responseFields.description: Description of the status for the entire request.

responseFields.name: subscriptionStatus
responseFields.description: Resulting subscription state, for example REGISTERED or UNREGISTERED. This — not an error code — is how you confirm the outcome, so read it on every response.

responseHandling.outcome: The request was processed. Whether the subscriber is now opted in is in subscriptionStatus, not in statusCode.
persist: subscriptionStatus, with the consent record that authorised the call
responseHandling.next: Compare subscriptionStatus by prefix, trimmed and upper-cased — the published samples carry a trailing dot. REGISTERED means opted in, including on a repeat call. Any other value, such as REG_PENDING or INITIAL, is not active yet: do not deliver the service until the subscriber notification reports REGISTERED.

wrongFields.subscriberIds: Register takes one subscriber, as subscriberId — a single tel: string, not an array.
wrongFields.msisdn: The subscriber goes in subscriberId, as tel:880….

rules: Capture explicit consent before every register, and store who consented, when, through which channel, and the exact wording shown.
Disclose the amount, currency and frequency before subscribing anyone.

Applink publishes no 'already registered' benign code. Make register idempotent by reading subscriptionStatus in the response instead of special-casing an error code — a repeat register that comes back REGISTERED is the state you wanted.
Mirror subscription state in your own database from the subscription notification callback rather than re-querying per request.

services.name: Subscription Unregister
services.summary: Opt a subscriber out of the application. Same endpoint as register, with action "0".

parameters.name: applicationId
parameters.description: Identifies the application. Unique identifier generated when the application is provisioned. Only a single value per request.

parameters.name: password
parameters.description: The API key sent to your registered email address when the application was approved.

parameters.name: subscriberId
parameters.description: The subscriber's tel:-prefixed MSISDN, a unique identifier. May be a masked value depending on the application type. Only a single value per request.

parameters.name: action
parameters.description: 0 = user unsubscription, 1 = user subscription. Sent as a string.

responseFields.name: version
responseFields.description: API version.

responseFields.name: statusCode
responseFields.description: The status code for the entire request.

responseFields.name: statusDetail
responseFields.description: Description of the status for the entire request. The documented sample carries "not registered" alongside S1000 — success here means the request was processed, not that a change occurred.

responseFields.name: subscriptionStatus
responseFields.description: Resulting subscription state, for example UNREGISTERED. Read it to confirm the outcome.

responseHandling.outcome: The request was processed. Whether the subscriber is now opted out is in subscriptionStatus, not in statusCode or statusDetail.
persist: subscriptionStatus, and cancel anything queued for this subscriber
responseHandling.next: Compare subscriptionStatus by prefix, trimmed and upper-cased — the published sample is "UNREGISTERED." with a trailing dot. UNREGISTERED is the desired state whether or not the subscriber was registered before, so statusDetail "not registered" alongside it is still success.

wrongFields.subscriberIds: Unregister takes one subscriber, as subscriberId — a single tel: string, not an array.
wrongFields.msisdn: The subscriber goes in subscriberId, as tel:880….

rules: Opting out must be as easy as opting in — offer it over MO SMS keywords (STOP, UNSUB, OFF), in a USSD menu option, and in-app.
Honour an opt-out immediately, including cancelling messages already queued or scheduled for that subscriber.
Unregistering someone who was never registered is not an error: the documented sample returns S1000 with subscriptionStatus UNREGISTERED. Treat reaching the desired state as success.
Never re-subscribe a subscriber who opted out without a fresh, separately recorded opt-in.

services.name: Base Size
services.summary: Return the number of subscribers currently registered to the application.

parameters.name: applicationId
parameters.description: Identifies the application. Unique identifier generated when the application is provisioned. Only a single value per request.

parameters.name: password
parameters.description: The API key sent to your registered email address when the application was approved.

responseFields.name: baseSize
responseFields.description: Number of registered users. Arrives as a string — coerce it before arithmetic or charting.

responseFields.name: version
responseFields.description: API version.

responseFields.name: statusCode
responseFields.description: The status code for the entire request.

responseFields.name: statusDetail
responseFields.description: Description of the status for the entire request.

responseHandling.outcome: Credentials, provisioning and the egress IP all work, and baseSize is the current count of registered subscribers.
persist: baseSize, parsed to an integer, into your metrics store
responseHandling.next: Parse baseSize as an integer — it arrives as a string. A base of "0" is a valid answer for a new application, not an error.

wrongFields.subscriberId: Base Size takes no subscriber. The body is only applicationId and password.

rules: This is the cheapest call on the platform — no subscriber, no charge, no side effect. Use it as the connectivity, credential and IP-whitelist smoke test.
baseSize is a string. Parse it.
It is a point-in-time count for the whole application, not a per-operator or per-segment figure.
Poll it on a schedule into your own metrics store rather than per page load, and sanity-check it before any tel:all broadcast.

services.name: Get Subscriber Charging Info
services.summary: Look up subscription status and last-charge details for up to ten subscribers in one request.

parameters.name: applicationId
parameters.description: Identifies the application. Unique identifier generated when the application is provisioned. Only a single value per request.

parameters.name: password
parameters.description: The API key sent to your registered email address when the application was approved.

parameters.name: subscriberIds
parameters.description: MSISDNs of the subscribers to look up, as tel:-prefixed values. If the application accepts masked numbers, the masked values go here. Maximum ten per request.

responseFields.name: version
responseFields.description: API version.

responseFields.name: destinationResponses
responseFields.description: One entry per subscriber in the request. Which fields are present depends on the subscription status — INITIAL and REG_PENDING omit the charge fields.

fields.name: subscriberId
fields.description: MSISDN of the subscriber, masked if the application uses masked numbers.

fields.name: subscriptionStatus
fields.description: One of INITIAL, REG_PENDING, TRIAL, REGISTERED, UNREGISTERED or TEMPORARY_BLOCKED.

fields.name: lastChargedDate
fields.description: Date of the last successful charge, formatted YYYY-MM-DD hh:mm:ss. Omitted for a free application.

fields.name: lastChargedAmount
fields.description: Amount of the last successful charge with its currency code. Sent as 0.00 for a free application.

fields.name: numberType
fields.description: Whether the subscriber is prepaid or postpaid.

fields.name: statusCode
fields.description: Success or error code for this subscriber.

fields.name: statusDetail
fields.description: Human-readable outcome for this subscriber.

responseFields.name: statusCode
responseFields.description: The status code for the entire request.

responseFields.name: statusDetail
responseFields.description: Description of the status for the entire request.

responseHandling.outcome: The lookup ran. The answer for each subscriber is in its own destinationResponses entry.
persist: each entry's subscriptionStatus into your local mirror, keyed by subscriberId
responseHandling.next: Iterate destinationResponses and branch on each entry's statusCode. REGISTERED or TRIAL means the subscription is usable; INITIAL and REG_PENDING are not yet, and carry no lastCharged fields — read those with a default.

wrongFields.subscriberId: Get Subscriber Charging Info takes subscriberIds — plural, an array of up to ten tel: addresses — even for one subscriber.

rules: This is Applink's subscription-status lookup — there is no separate getStatus endpoint. Use it for reconciliation, not as a per-request gate.
Maximum ten MSISDNs per request. Batch larger sets with your own throttle.
The published request schema names the required field subscriberId while the property it documents is subscriberIds. Send subscriberIds — the array — as the sample does.
The published sample writes the array entries with a stray space after tel:. Send tel:8801973579363 with no space.
Branch on each entry's statusCode, not only the top-level one.
REG_PENDING and INITIAL mean the subscription is not usable yet. Do not start delivering the service until the status is REGISTERED or TRIAL.

services.name: Request OTP
services.summary: Send a one-time password to a subscriber's MSISDN so they can activate a subscription from a web or mobile app.

parameters.name: applicationId
parameters.description: Identifies the application. Unique identifier generated when the application is provisioned. Only a single value per request.

parameters.name: password
parameters.description: The API key sent to your registered email address when the application was approved.

parameters.name: subscriberId
parameters.description: Mobile number of the subscriber, in the format tel:8801416177301.

parameters.name: applicationHash
parameters.description: Hash string that determines which verification messages to send to your app.

parameters.name: applicationMetaData
parameters.exampleNote: describes your client — send it with your own values or leave it out
parameters.description: Client context for the request: client (web browser or mobile app), device (iPhone 6, Galaxy S5, PC…), os (Android 6, iOS 5, Windows 10…) and appCode (the store identifier for an app, or the web link for a browser).

fields.name: client
fields.description: Client type. Values are a web browser or a mobile app.

fields.name: device
fields.description: Type or OS of the device — iPhone 6, Galaxy S5, PC and so on.

fields.name: os
fields.description: OS or device version — Android 6, iOS 5, Windows 10 and so on.

fields.name: appCode
fields.description: Your app identifier in the store if you use an app, or the web link if you use a browser.

responseFields.name: version
responseFields.description: API version.

responseFields.name: statusCode
responseFields.description: The status code for the entire request. S1000 when the OTP challenge was sent.

responseFields.name: referenceNo
responseFields.description: Reference key that uniquely identifies the request. Keep it server-side against the user's session — it is what /otp/verify is called with.

responseFields.name: statusDetail
responseFields.description: The status detail for the entire request.

responseHandling.outcome: The OTP is on its way to the subscriber's phone.
persist: referenceNo — server-side, in the user's session, for five minutes; never sent to the client
responseHandling.next: Collect the OTP the subscriber types in, then call Verify OTP with this referenceNo.

wrongFields.subscriberIds: Request OTP takes one subscriber, as subscriberId — a single tel: string.
wrongFields.metaData: The field is applicationMetaData — an object of strings (client, device, os, appCode). Omit it entirely rather than sending it empty.

rules: Rate-limit OTP requests yourself, per number and per IP. Without it the application becomes an SMS-bombing tool aimed at arbitrary Bangladeshi numbers, at your expense.
referenceNo lives server-side, in the session. Never send it to the client, never put it in a URL, and never let the client choose it.
Never log the OTP or the referenceNo.
Call this from the backend only — the platform enforces IP whitelisting that a browser or mobile client cannot satisfy.

services.name: Verify OTP
services.summary: Verify an OTP the subscriber typed in. On success the Applink subscription is activated and the subscriberId is returned.

parameters.name: applicationId
parameters.description: Identifies the application. Unique identifier generated when the application is provisioned. Only a single value per request.

parameters.name: password
parameters.description: The API key sent to your registered email address when the application was approved.

parameters.name: referenceNo
parameters.description: Reference number returned by the Request OTP API. See the Request OTP response.

parameters.name: otp
parameters.description: The one-time password to use for MSISDN verification for this application.

responseFields.name: version
responseFields.description: API version.

responseFields.name: statusCode
responseFields.description: The status code for the entire request. S1000 when the OTP validated.

responseFields.name: subscriptionStatus
responseFields.description: Subscription status of the user — INITIAL or REGISTERED.

responseFields.name: statusDetail
responseFields.description: The status detail for the entire request.

responseFields.name: subscriberId
responseFields.description: The subscriber's mobile number, plain or masked depending on whether the application is set up for plain or masked number usage. Store this — it is the identity used by every later Applink call.

responseHandling.outcome: The OTP validated and the subscription was activated.
persist: subscriberId — exactly as returned; it may be masked, and it is the identity for every later Applink call
responseHandling.next: Store subscriberId against your user. E1850 means re-prompt against the same referenceNo; E1851 means the OTP expired and a new one must be requested.

wrongFields.requestCorrelator: Verify OTP takes referenceNo, and it is the referenceNo from Request OTP. requestCorrelator belongs to the CaaS charging flow.
wrongFields.subscriberId: Verify OTP does not take the subscriber — only referenceNo and otp. The subscriberId comes back in the response.
wrongFields.code: The OTP the subscriber typed goes in otp, as a string.

rules: The OTP is valid for five minutes. Expire it on your side too rather than relying on the platform.
Store the returned subscriberId as the user's identity for every later Applink call. It may be masked; treat it as opaque.
E1850 (invalid OTP), E1851 (expired) and E1855 (invalid reference number) are user-facing prompts, not retries.
Cap verification attempts per referenceNo on your side and force a fresh request after that.

services.name: CaaS OTP Generation
services.summary: Start a one-time charge against a subscriber's mobile account. Applink sends an OTP to the subscriber, who must enter it before the charge completes.

parameters.name: applicationId
parameters.description: Identifies the application. Unique identifier generated when the application is provisioned. Only a single value per request.

parameters.name: password
parameters.description: The API key sent to your registered email address when the application was approved.

parameters.name: externalTrxId
parameters.description: The transaction ID generated by the application to map the request to the response. It is what support and reconciliation trace on. Only a single value per request.

parameters.name: amount
parameters.description: Amount to be reserved for charging, sent as a string. Only a single value per request.

parameters.name: paymentInstrumentName
parameters.description: The name of the payment instrument, for example Mobile Account. Only a single value per request.

parameters.name: subscriberId
parameters.description: The tel:-prefixed MSISDN of the subscriber to be charged. May be a masked value depending on the application type. Only a single value per request.

parameters.name: Currency
parameters.description: Currency unit of the amount. Only BDT is allowed. Note the capital C — this is how the parameter is published, and it differs from the lower-case currency used by Query Balance.

responseFields.name: timeStamp
responseFields.description: The time the request was sent.

responseFields.name: externalTrxId
responseFields.description: Echo of the transaction ID you generated. Assert it matches what you sent.

responseFields.name: statusDetail
responseFields.description: Detailed description explaining the status of the entire request.

responseFields.name: requestCorrelator
responseFields.description: The unique identifier used internally to identify the transaction. This is the value you must pass as referenceNo to CaaS OTP Verification — persist it with the pending charge.

responseFields.name: internalTrxId
responseFields.description: The transaction ID generated by the service provider, used to track the transaction. Persist it for support.

responseFields.name: statusCode
responseFields.description: Status of the request. A leading P means partial, E means error and S means success. P1003 means the OTP is on its way and the charge is not complete.

sampleResponse.statusDetail: Request successfully proceed. OTP will send to user.

responseHandling.outcome: P1003 is the expected answer: the OTP was sent to the subscriber and nothing has been charged. S1000 is in this endpoint's published code list too — if it ever arrives here, handle it exactly like P1003: pending, never charged.
persist: requestCorrelator — on the PENDING ledger row; it is the referenceNo step two needs and cannot be recovered
responseHandling.next: Assert the echoed externalTrxId equals the one you sent. Prompt the subscriber for the OTP, then call CaaS OTP Verification with referenceNo = requestCorrelator and sourceAddress = this subscriberId. Fulfil nothing yet.

wrongFields.currency: CaaS OTP Generation spells it Currency — capital C. Lower-case currency is the Query Balance parameter.
wrongFields.referenceNo: There is no referenceNo on this call. The platform returns requestCorrelator, which you then send as referenceNo to CaaS OTP Verification.
wrongFields.subscriberIds: The subscriber goes in subscriberId — a single tel: string.

rules: This is step one of two. Nothing is deducted until the subscriber's OTP is verified through CaaS OTP Verification.
externalTrxId is your idempotency key. Generate it, persist it with a PENDING charge row BEFORE sending, and reuse it unchanged on any resolution attempt.
Persist requestCorrelator from the response — it is the referenceNo the verification step needs, and it is not recoverable if you drop it.
P1003 is not success. It means the OTP was dispatched. The charge is settled by the charging notification callback, not by this response.
Never retry with a fresh externalTrxId. A timeout does not mean the charge did not start.
Hold amounts in a decimal type in your own code. Amount and currency come from server-side configuration, never from client input.
Only BDT is allowed, and the parameter is spelled Currency with a capital C.

services.name: CaaS OTP Verification
services.summary: Verify the OTP the subscriber entered and complete the one-time charge against their mobile account.

parameters.name: applicationId
parameters.description: Identifies the application. Unique identifier generated when the application is provisioned. Only a single value per request.

parameters.name: password
parameters.description: The API key sent to your registered email address when the application was approved.

parameters.name: referenceNo
parameters.description: The value returned as requestCorrelator in the CaaS OTP Generation response. It is the reference of the transaction.

parameters.name: otp
parameters.description: The OTP the subscriber entered into the developer application.

parameters.name: sourceAddress
parameters.description: The tel:-prefixed MSISDN that requested the OTP — the subscriber being charged.

responseFields.name: statusCode
responseFields.description: The status code for the request. The published sample for this endpoint echoes the request body rather than showing a response envelope, so read statusCode and statusDetail and treat the charging notification as the authoritative outcome.

responseFields.name: statusDetail
responseFields.description: Description of the status for the request.

responseHandling.outcome: The OTP was accepted and the charge submitted. It is not settled until the charging notification arrives.
persist: the ledger row's state — verified, awaiting the charging notification
responseHandling.next: Fulfil only when the charging notification for this externalTrxId arrives with statusCode S1000 and a paidAmount that covers the amount. E1850 means re-prompt against the same referenceNo; never re-run CaaS OTP Generation.

wrongFields.requestCorrelator: Send the requestCorrelator value as referenceNo — that is the field name this endpoint takes.
wrongFields.externalTrxId: Not a parameter here. referenceNo is the requestCorrelator from CaaS OTP Generation, never your externalTrxId.
wrongFields.subscriberId: This endpoint names the subscriber sourceAddress — the same tel: value you sent as subscriberId to CaaS OTP Generation.

rules: This is the step that deducts money. Everything before it only reserved an intent.
referenceNo is the requestCorrelator from CaaS OTP Generation, not the externalTrxId you generated.

Never re-run the generation step to 'retry' a failed verification — that starts a second charge. Prompt the subscriber for the OTP again against the same referenceNo, or abandon the transaction and reconcile.
Settle the ledger row from the charging notification callback, which carries paidAmount, balanceDue and the final statusCode. Do not treat this response as the last word.
Never log the OTP or the referenceNo.

The published response sample for this endpoint repeats the request fields. Read statusCode and statusDetail, and log the whole body once in Limited Production so you know what your account actually returns.

services.name: Query Balance
services.summary: Read a subscriber's chargeable balance, account type and account status before attempting a charge.
services.requiresProvisioning: balance queries enabled on the application's CaaS configuration

parameters.name: applicationId
parameters.description: Identifies the application. Unique identifier generated when the application is provisioned. Only a single value per request.

parameters.name: password
parameters.description: The API key sent to your registered email address when the application was approved.

parameters.name: subscriberId
parameters.description: The MSISDN or username of the subscriber whose account balance is being queried. May be a masked value depending on the application type. Only a single value per request.

parameters.name: paymentInstrumentName
parameters.description: The name of the payment instrument. Only a single value per request.

parameters.name: accountId
parameters.description: The account of the payment instrument. Only a single value per request.

parameters.name: currency
parameters.description: Currency unit of the amount. Only BDT is allowed. Note the lower-case c, unlike the Currency parameter on CaaS OTP Generation.

responseFields.name: accountType
responseFields.description: Account type of the subscriber ID, for example Pre Paid or Post Paid.

responseFields.name: accountStatus
responseFields.description: Account status of the subscriber ID.

responseFields.name: chargeableBalance
responseFields.description: Available chargeable balance of the subscriber: remaining account balance for a prepaid user, or credit limit minus outstanding bill for a postpaid user. Rounded to two decimal points and sent as a string.

responseFields.name: statusCode
responseFields.description: The status code for the entire request.

responseFields.name: statusDetail
responseFields.description: Description of the status for the entire request.

responseHandling.outcome: chargeableBalance is what the subscriber can be charged right now.
responseHandling.next: Parse chargeableBalance into a decimal type — it arrives as a string. It is advisory: E1326 can still come back from the charge itself.

wrongFields.Currency: Query Balance spells it currency — lower-case c. Capital-C Currency is the CaaS OTP Generation parameter.
wrongFields.subscriberIds: The subscriber goes in subscriberId — a single tel: string.

rules: This endpoint is in the published API specification but is not listed in the rendered documentation's navigation. Confirm with support that it is enabled on your application before you depend on it.
A balance check is advisory, not a reservation. The balance can change between this call and the charge — always handle E1326 on the charging path regardless of what this returned.
chargeableBalance is a string. Parse it into a decimal type, never a binary float you then compare for equality.
Leaving APPLINK_CAAS_BALANCE_URL unset is how you disable this locally on an application that does not have it.

callbacks.name: SMS Receive (MO)
callbacks.configuredIn: SMS API settings — the MO / receive URL
callbacks.summary: Fires when a subscriber sends an SMS to your shortcode with your keyword.

fields.name: version
fields.description: API version, numbered 1.0, 2.0 and so on.

fields.name: applicationId
fields.description: Your application ID. Verify it matches before doing anything with the payload.

fields.name: sourceAddress
fields.description: Address of the sender, masked if number masking is enabled on the application.

fields.name: message
fields.description: Content of the message sent by the user, including the keyword that routed it to you.

fields.name: requestId
fields.description: Uniquely identifies this request within the platform. This is the deduplication key.

fields.name: encoding
fields.description: Encoding scheme used in the message. 0 = Text, 240 = Flash SMS, 245 = Binary, in which case the content is hex encoded.

rules: The message arrives with the keyword included. Trim, collapse whitespace and compare the keyword case-insensitively.
Recognise the standard opt-out words — STOP, UNSUB, OFF — and honour them by calling Subscription Unregister.
An MO SMS is not authenticated beyond the source address. Never perform a destructive or chargeable action on the strength of one.
Never echo user content back into an outbound SMS without sanitising it.

callbacks.name: SMS Delivery Status Report
callbacks.configuredIn: SMS API settings — the delivery report URL
callbacks.summary: Fires when an MT SMS sent with deliveryStatusRequest "1" reaches a final state at the message centre.

fields.name: destinationAddress
fields.description: Address of the subscriber the report is about.

fields.name: timeStamp
fields.description: The timestamp sent from the SMS, documented as yyMMddHHmm — yy last two digits of the year, MM month 01-12, dd day 01-31, HH hour 00-23, mm minute 00-59. The published sample is 14 digits, so parse on length rather than assuming one form.

fields.name: requestId
fields.description: Uniquely identifies the request within the platform. Match it against the requestId returned by the original SMS Send.

fields.name: deliveryStatus
fields.description: Final state of the message as reported by the platform to the application.

rules: ACCEPTED is not DELIVERED — it means the network took the message, nothing more.
Reports arrive out of order, late, more than once, or never. Store the latest status keyed by requestId and keep the handler idempotent.
Repeated UNDELIVERABLE for one subscriber usually means a dead number. Stop messaging it rather than paying for nothing.
The underlying SMPP layer uses abbreviated spellings such as DELIVRD, UNDELIV, ACCEPTD and REJECTD. Normalise both forms on the way in.

callbacks.name: USSD Receive
callbacks.configuredIn: USSD API settings — the receive URL
callbacks.summary: Fires when a subscriber dials your USSD code or presses a key inside an open session.

fields.name: version
fields.description: API version, numbered 1.0, 2.0 and so on.

fields.name: applicationId
fields.description: Your application ID. Verify it matches.

fields.name: message
fields.description: Content of the message sent by the user — the code they dialled or the key they pressed.

fields.name: requestId
fields.description: Uniquely identifies this request within the platform. This is the deduplication key.

fields.name: sessionId
fields.description: Unique number the USSD gateway assigns to the application for the duration of the session, maintained across every message in that session. Echo it on every USSD Send.

fields.name: ussdOperation
fields.description: USSD operation. Inbound you will see mo-init when the subscriber starts the session and mo-cont for each message after it.

fields.name: sourceAddress
fields.description: Address of the sender, masked if number masking is enabled on the application.

fields.name: vlrAddress
fields.description: VLR (Visitor Location Register) address of the sender.

fields.name: encoding
fields.description: Encoding scheme used in the message. 440 = plain ASCII characters.

rules: The body you return is an acknowledgement, not a reply. The screen the subscriber sees comes from a separate POST to /ussd/send.
Acknowledge before doing any work — USSD sessions time out in seconds.
Key session state on the platform's sessionId, with a TTL of about two minutes, in a store shared across every instance.
mo-init starts a session; mo-cont continues one. Nothing tells you the path the user took to get here except your own session state.

callbacks.name: Subscriber Notification
callbacks.configuredIn: Subscription API settings — the notification URL
callbacks.summary: Fires when a subscription changes — including changes you did not initiate, such as a subscriber texting STOP or a recurring charge failing.

fields.name: timeStamp
fields.description: The timestamp sent from the SMS, documented as yyMMddHHmm — yy last two digits of the year, MM month 01-12, dd day 01-31, HH hour 00-23, mm minute 00-59. The published sample is 14 digits, so parse on length.

fields.name: version
fields.description: API version, numbered 1.0, 2.0 and so on.

fields.name: applicationId
fields.description: Your application ID. Verify it matches.

fields.name: password
fields.description: Your API key, sent by the platform inside the notification. Never log this field, and if you compare it, compare it in constant time.

fields.name: subscriberId
fields.description: The subscriber's tel:-prefixed MSISDN, a unique identifier. May be a masked value depending on the application type.

fields.name: frequency
fields.description: Frequency at which notifications are sent for this subscription.

fields.name: status
fields.description: Status of the subscription, for example UNREGISTERED or REGISTERED.

rules: This callback is the authoritative source of subscription state. Consuming it is what lets you keep a local mirror instead of re-querying.
It carries your password in the body. Never log the raw payload, and redact that field before anything reaches a log aggregator.
A notification is not authorisation. Reconcile against your own records before unlocking a paid feature.
Deduplicate on subscriberId, status and timeStamp together — the same change can be delivered more than once.

callbacks.name: Charging Notification
callbacks.configuredIn: CaaS API settings — the charging notification URL
callbacks.summary: Fires automatically when a charging transaction completes. There is nothing to call — it is the callback that settles the charge you started.

fields.name: timeStamp
fields.description: The time the request was sent. The published sample is formatted 15-Nov-2023 11:55, which is not the format any other Applink field uses — parse defensively.

fields.name: TotalAmount
fields.description: Amount deducted from the subscriber as the one-time charge. Note the capital T — this is how the field is published.

fields.name: externalTrxId
fields.description: The transaction ID your application generated for the charge. This is how you match the notification to your ledger row.

fields.name: balanceDue
fields.description: The amount still due, if any. Shows 0 when nothing is outstanding.

fields.name: statusDetail
fields.description: Detailed description explaining the status of the entire request.

fields.name: currency
fields.description: Currency unit of the amount. Only BDT is allowed.

fields.name: version
fields.description: API version, numbered 1.0, 2.0 and so on.

fields.name: internalTrxId
fields.description: The unique identifier used to track the request at the developer application end.

fields.name: paidAmount
fields.description: The amount actually paid by the subscriber. Compare it against what you charged before marking the order fulfilled.

fields.name: referenceId
fields.description: The unique reference used to identify the transaction within the system.

fields.name: statusCode
fields.description: Status of the request. A leading P means partial, E means error and S means success.

samplePayload.statusDetail: Request was Successfully processed, Due amount fully paid.

rules: This is your reconciliation channel. Every charge your code left in an unknown state after a timeout is resolved here.
Match on externalTrxId — the key you generated and persisted before starting the charge.
Deduplicate on externalTrxId and statusCode together. A repeat notification for an already-settled transaction must not double-count revenue.
Compare paidAmount and balanceDue against your ledger before treating an order as fulfilled — a partial payment is a real outcome.
TotalAmount carries a capital T while paidAmount and balanceDue do not. Bind the field names exactly.

pending.action: The platform accepted the request but the outcome is not settled. Do not re-send it. Continue the flow — for a charge, collect the OTP and call CaaS OTP Verification — and settle from the charging notification.

configuration.action: Provisioning or credentials are wrong. Fix it in the portal — code changes will not help. Alert on these in production; the integration is down, not one request.

client.action: Your payload is wrong, or the user gave bad input. Fix the request or prompt the user.

user-state.action: The subscriber is not eligible right now. Communicate; do not retry in a loop.

transient.action: Platform-side. Exponential backoff with jitter, capped attempts, then dead-letter.

S1000.description: Process completed successfully for all the available destination numbers.

P1003.description: Request successfully processed. The OTP will be sent to the subscriber.
P1003.fix: CaaS OTP Generation succeeded and nothing has been charged yet. Persist requestCorrelator, collect the OTP from the subscriber, and call CaaS OTP Verification with it.

E1301.description: Requested ApplicationID is not allowed within the system for the operator.
E1301.fix: The application is not enabled for this operator. Check the provisioning record in the portal.

E1303.description: The IP address this request originated from is not provisioned to send requests to the application. Use a provisioned system, or ask the administrator to provision the new IP.
E1303.fix: Find the real egress IP by running curl -4 https://api.ipify.org on the calling server, then add it to the application's allowed host addresses in the portal.

E1308.description: Permanent charging error — the platform supplies the reason, for example insufficient balance.
E1308.fix: Permanent for this attempt. Do not blind-retry; read statusDetail, tell the subscriber, and settle the ledger row from the charging notification.

E1309.description: The requested service is not allowed for this application.
E1309.fix: That API was not provisioned for this application. A portal fix, not a code fix.

E1311.description: Mobile terminated SMS messages are not enabled. Check the NCS configuration in provisioning.

E1312.description: The request is invalid — typically a missing mandatory field or a malformed value.
E1312.fix: Compare the payload against the parameter table for that endpoint. `applink validate <id> '<json>'` catches most causes.

E1313.description: Authentication failed. There is no active application with that applicationId, no active service provider, or the password in the request is invalid.
E1313.fix: Check APPLINK_APP_ID and APPLINK_PASSWORD, and that the application is active in the portal.

E1315.description: Cannot find the requested service, or it is not active.

E1317.description: The MSISDN in the request is invalid or not allowed.
E1317.fix: Validate the number before sending. Do not retry the same value.

E1318.description: The transaction limit per second has been exceeded. Throttle requests, or ask the administrator to raise the traffic limit.
E1318.fix: Add a client-side rate limiter. Backoff will clear it; more concurrency will not.

E1319.description: The transaction limit for today has been exceeded. Try again tomorrow, or ask the administrator to raise the per-day limit.
E1319.fix: Retrying today will not help. Queue the work and alert — this is a capacity problem, not a request problem.

E1325.description: The format of the address is invalid. The expected format is a tel:-prefixed MSISDN.
E1325.fix: A missing tel: prefix, or a stray space. Normalise every address through one helper.

E1326.fix: Tell the subscriber. Retry later if they top up, never in a loop.

E1328.description: The charging operation is not allowed. Check the NCS configuration.

E1331.description: The source address is not allowed. Use one of the values configured in the alias configuration in the SLAs, or send the request without a sourceAddress so the platform uses the default sender address.
E1331.fix: sourceAddress must be a provisioned alias, or omitted entirely.

E1334.description: The message could not be processed because its length is too long. The platform supplies the maximum.
E1334.fix: Shorten or split the message. Bangla text is UCS-2, so the per-part budget is 70 characters, not 160.

E1335.description: The message could not be processed because the advertisement message length is too long. The platform supplies the maximum.

E1337.fix: The platform already has a transaction with this identifier. Do NOT generate a fresh externalTrxId — that starts a second charge. Resolve the outcome of the original from the charging notification.

E1341.description: The request failed. Errors occurred while sending the request for all the destinations.

E1342.description: The MSISDN is blacklisted and is not authorised to use this application.
E1342.fix: Stop messaging this subscriber. Nothing in your code will change the outcome.

E1343.description: The MSISDN is not whitelisted. Only whitelisted numbers are allowed to send messages at this stage.
E1343.fix: While the application is in Limited Production only numbers on the whitelist can use it. Add the test number in the portal.

E1601.description: The system experienced an unexpected error.

E1603.description: A temporary system error occurred while delivering your request.

E1850.fix: Prompt the subscriber to re-enter it. Cap the attempts yourself and force a fresh OTP request after that.

E1851.fix: An Applink OTP is valid for five minutes. Request a new one.

E1855.fix: referenceNo must be the value returned by the matching request — referenceNo from Request OTP, or requestCorrelator from CaaS OTP Generation. It is not the externalTrxId you generated.

E1856.fix: Seen on the OTP endpoints. Check every mandatory field is present and correctly named before retrying.

practices.title: Never hardcode applicationId or password
practices.detail: Environment variables only, through one config module, validated at startup. Not in source, not in a client bundle, not in a committed file, not in a log, not in git history. Never prefixed NEXT_PUBLIC_ / VITE_ / REACT_APP_.

practices.title: Never call Applink from client-side code
practices.detail: Clients call your backend; your backend calls Applink. The credentials are a shared secret and the platform enforces IP whitelisting, which a mobile client cannot satisfy.

practices.title: Explicit consent before register or charge
practices.detail: Record who consented, when, through which channel, and the exact wording shown. Disclose the amount, currency and frequency first. Applications are suspended over this.

practices.title: Charging must be idempotent
practices.detail: One externalTrxId per logical charge, persisted before the call and reused on any resolution attempt. Never re-roll it, and never re-run CaaS OTP Generation to retry a failed verification — either one starts a second charge against a real person.

practices.title: Branch on statusCode, not the HTTP status
practices.detail: Applink returns HTTP 200 for application-level failures. Checking res.ok reports failures as successes. S1000 is success; P1003 on CaaS OTP Generation means pending, not done.

practices.title: A charge is not complete until the OTP is verified
practices.detail: CaaS OTP Generation only dispatches an OTP and returns P1003. Money moves at CaaS OTP Verification, and the final outcome arrives on the charging notification callback. Code that treats the first response as a completed charge fulfils orders nobody paid for.

practices.title: Treat subscriberId as opaque
practices.detail: With masking enabled it is not a phone number. Do not parse it, strip it, or assume a length. Store and send back exactly what you received.

practices.title: Never ship disabled TLS verification
practices.detail: If a handshake fails on an incomplete certificate chain, supply the missing intermediate CA explicitly. Disabling verification exposes the credentials that can charge your subscribers.

practices.title: Acknowledge callbacks before doing work
practices.detail: Respond S1000 immediately, then process asynchronously. USSD sessions time out in seconds; slow handlers cause retries, duplicates and dropped sessions.

practices.title: Every callback handler must be idempotent
practices.detail: All five callbacks can arrive more than once. Deduplicate on the documented key. A duplicate charging notification that double-counts revenue is a real bug.

practices.title: Never trust the callback body
practices.detail: It is unauthenticated JSON from the public internet. Validate the schema, verify applicationId, restrict by source IP, rate-limit, and never treat a callback as authorisation.

practices.title: The subscription notification contains your password
practices.detail: Applink posts the applicationId and password into the subscriber notification body. Redact that field before the payload reaches any log, trace, error report or analytics sink, and compare it in constant time if you use it.

practices.title: A static egress IP is a hard requirement
practices.detail: IP whitelisting is enforced with E1303. Serverless platforms with rotating egress need a NAT gateway or a fixed-IP proxy. Decide before choosing a host.

practices.title: Guard tel:all
practices.detail: A broadcast to the entire subscriber base must never be reachable from an ordinary code path. Require an explicit, separately-authorised call and sanity-check against Base Size first.

practices.title: Subscription, OTP and CaaS are transactions, not a login API
practices.detail: These endpoints charge money, send paid SMS and consume the per-second and per-day transaction limits every time they run. Use them once, to bind a verified subscriberId to an account with recorded consent; then issue the application's own session and decide entitlement from the local subscription mirror. No Applink call belongs on a login or page-load path. Reserve a fresh OTP for genuine re-verification (new device, changed number, step-up), and never treat a live session as authorisation to charge.

practices.title: USSD session state must be shared across instances
practices.detail: An in-process map breaks the moment you scale horizontally or deploy. Use Redis or equivalent, with a TTL of about two minutes.

practices.title: Never log secrets or unmasked subscriber data
practices.detail: Log requestId, sessionId, externalTrxId, internalTrxId and statusCode. Never the password, the OTP, referenceNo, requestCorrelator, or an unmasked subscriberId. Mask in the logger, not at each call site.

practices.title: Set an explicit timeout on every call
practices.detail: Ten to fifteen seconds. No default-infinite requests.

practices.title: Retry only transient codes and transport errors
practices.detail: Exponential backoff with jitter, capped attempts, then dead-letter. Never retry a definitive E13xx, and never retry anything on the charging path with a new identifier.

practices.title: Mirror subscription state locally
practices.detail: Consume the subscriber notification callback instead of calling Get Subscriber Charging Info on every request — it is capped at ten MSISDNs per call and is meant for reconciliation. Store the status and when it was last confirmed, update it from the subscriber notification, and reconcile stale rows on a schedule (getSubscriberChargingInfo, maximum ten per call) rather than in the request path.

practices.title: Use a decimal type for money
practices.detail: Never a binary float. Amount and currency come from server-side configuration or a server-side price lookup, never from client input. Only BDT is accepted.
